drugs.dose: Weight-band dosing per national TB program
drugs.duration: 2 months intensive phase, then HR for 4-10 months continuation (total duration extended if CNS/bone involvement identified)
drugs.why: Standard four-drug regimen; duration should be extended if disseminated disease is found to involve the CNS or skeletal system on further workup, which would change the continuation phase length.

drugs.coverage: Used when resistance is identified or the patient fails to respond to first-line therapy.

framework: Make reasonable, parallel attempts at microbiological/histological confirmation (sputum, blood culture for AFB/mycobacterial blood culture, bone marrow or liver biopsy if indicated) but do not let this delay treatment in a deteriorating or critically ill patient with strong clinical suspicion.
Screen for and manage immunosuppressive causes (notably HIV) concurrently, since these significantly affect both presentation and treatment considerations (drug interactions, immune reconstitution).
Register and notify per national TB program requirements once treatment is started.
Evaluate for CNS and skeletal involvement specifically, as this extends required treatment duration beyond the standard 6 months.

references: National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP) India Guidelines
